title: Those Who Must Be Saved
text: The spear spirit really did send me flying to quite the outrageous point in time, I say. First, I needed to sort out the situation. While casually wrapping up conversations with villagers and drifting away from the village without drawing attention, I watched the young Big Sister playing innocently in the distance, and thought things over alone.

Hmm… Indeed, there were traces here and there that hinted at what would become of Big Sister’s village once it lay in ruins. There was no mistaking that the buildings that would later be destroyed now stood whole and unharmed.

What was I to do in a situation like this? Right, that was the thing. I now found myself at a point in time so far back that even wanting to return might not be possible. Whenever the others in past loops heard that I could loop, and asked how far back I could go, they always looked a little disappointed at my answer. That was because the starting point of my loops was always the moment right after the summoning, when I was at the castle together with Father and the others. It was easy enough to imagine the others listening to my account, half-envious, wishing they could ask me for something but unable to, given how far back that moment was. The villagers especially showed it plainly.

The most recent memory I had was… the wolf man? The name floated up faintly in my mind, but… if I recalled correctly, he’d mentioned this was long before the waves began, so it was likely earlier than even this point. …If I remembered right, it was something about wanting to avoid Takt killing his older brother, the Claw Hero. Takt, was it? Hm? I felt like something had happened involving him, but my memory was hazy on it. In any case, that fellow was a problem—he’d killed a Seven Star Hero and stolen and hidden the weapon—so dealing with him swiftly was the standard move. That much wasn’t going to change… but hmm. I felt like there was some other reason too, but I just couldn’t recall it, argh…

Well, forcing myself to remember something I couldn’t remember rarely worked out well, so I decided to shift my focus. In any case, I was now in a timeline that came before the misfortune that befell Big Sister, Older Sister, and the other villagers. What should I do in a situation like this…? Naturally, there weren’t all that many options. I wanted to somehow erase the damage done to this village. Not because doing so would necessarily lead to a better outcome in the end, but simply because avoiding tragedy was worth doing for its own sake. And more than that… well, somehow I felt like even back in the world I originally came from, before coming to this one, I’d experienced a similar sort of time loop.

No, actually—according to Ark, back in Japan I’d apparently been some kind of existence doomed to endlessly repeat romances with pigs, so maybe that was why this all felt like déjà vu. Anyway, that was the priority I’d settled on in my heart, but now I had to consider how things would change as a result.

What had the spear spirit said again? That this was something like a bonus stage. And that I’d been able to jump into this loop by using some exception handling Ark had set up for me… If I made a fatal mistake, could I return? That was the question. I’d need to ask the spear spirit about that, but for now I ought to act under the assumption that I couldn’t. To begin with, resetting things just because I didn’t like the outcome wasn’t really in my dictionary. More than that, I understood that since this all branched off from here, there was no such thing as a reset to begin with. Even if I had regrets, the world kept moving forward.

Just like that world where Rival stole Father away from me! Even if I could return to that branching point, it wouldn’t erase the fact that such a world—one where he’d been taken—had existed. That much wouldn’t change. So then, I couldn’t act on the assumption that I might make a mistake. Always giving my all to whatever I faced—that was who I was!

So then… let me think about what would happen if I saved this village—no, this whole region. That person Trash, who’d been at the castle, consulted with, and whom Éclair had sent off—I didn’t recognize that person, but they seemed to be someone important, apparently Éclair’s parent. Indeed, because that person died in the wave, Trash had been forced to govern Melromarc in the queen’s absence. If that person survived… the runaway excesses of the Three Heroes Church and Trash could probably be curbed to some degree. And following on from that… the Hero Summoning. It was the runaway excesses of the Three Heroes Church and Trash that had triggered the summoning of me, Father, Ren, and Itsuki together. Which meant, if the damage to this region were minimized and Éclair’s parent survived… then whether the Hero Summoning would even happen in Melromarc at all became uncertain. In other words, there was a chance Father and the others wouldn’t be summoned at all. A chance the world might be judged not to be under enough of a threat to warrant it.

In my mind’s eye rose the image of Father—excited about being summoned to another world, chatting with me and Ren and Itsuki, then looking a little dejected at how carelessly the people of the castle treated him. And of course, there was also the Father who wore a pained expression through the false accusations that followed, the Father who suffered even after I tried to help him. Perhaps, in this loop, I might not even get to meet Father at all. Think, Motoyasu. If I saved the village and its people before me, I might never meet Father. And what’s more, I’d certainly never meet Filo-tan either. That possibility existed too. …I could almost hear a voice whispering to me, telling me to let the wave happen, just to guarantee meeting Father. And indeed, that might well be the surer path.
“But… that’s not a choice I want to make, I say.”

Demanding Big Sister and the others’ tears as the minimum sacrifice needed just to meet Father. Right now, I was in a position to save everyone, and yet choosing not to do so… wouldn’t that leave me with even greater regret? I’d already resolved myself to endure any number of regrets, but I had no intention of turning a blind eye to the tragedy right in front of me just to spare myself one. And so—even if it meant never meeting Father. Precisely because this was a single, one-time chance, all the more reason. Father, I’m sorry, I say. This Motoyasu must act to prevent Father from ever being summoned, all in order to avert this tragedy. The moment I thought that, the kind Father from my memories smiled at me. That’s just like you, Motoyasu-kun, isn’t it? he seemed to say. Even the Father I hadn’t been able to save, in some other timeline, seemed to snort with a laugh, as if acknowledging that charging straight ahead like this was just so like me. Oh, Father. I do wish you’d approve of my engagement to Filo-tan. In this loop, I might never meet either of you. Whether I, going forward, could endure that, I didn’t know, but I resolved to do my best regardless. Now that that was decided, next I had to think about what to do.
About five days before the wave.

Should I just wait for the wave to arrive as usual, and the moment it appeared, use Aiming Lancer to pierce through every last monster and end it there? That would certainly work, I thought, but I had this much time on my hands. And more than that, it would draw far too much attention. Would that really eliminate all the damage? Not doing what could be done was, frankly, the height of waste.

To begin with, while the damage to the village was indeed caused by the wave, there must have been considerable damage from other causes as well. I needed to recall all of it. The first thing that came to mind was Big Sister’s parents dying. As far as I understood, they’d died right at the site of the wave. As for why Older Sister hadn’t been in the village during the wave… if I recalled correctly, she’d gone out for deep-sea fishing.

Most likely… she’d gone along with fishing that Trash had requested, hadn’t she? Older Sister was a fisherwoman, and this village had originally been a fishing village. Indeed, there were plenty of boats along the shore. And because the wave had churned up the sea, it had taken time to return—if I recalled, aside from Older Sister, none of the other villagers who’d gone out fishing that day had ever come back. That was how rough the sea had gotten for a while. Even the boat ride to Cal Mira Island had been rather rough, but this must have surpassed even that. Incidentally, I recalled Big Sister, who’d been aboard that boat at the time, seeming rather unbothered by it all, so it must truly have been quite the storm.
